name: Comic book halftone
means: Four-colour newsprint comic art: heavy black ink outline and solid spot blacks carrying the drawing, colour laid in as visible Ben-Day dot screens rather than solid fills, and the plates slightly out of register so a thin cyan or magenta fringe shows along the black line.
prose: a 1970s four-colour comic book page printed on newsprint, heavy black ink outlines and solid spot blacks, colour applied as coarse visible Ben-Day halftone dots rather than flat fills, the colour plates slightly misregistered so thin cyan and magenta fringes show against the black line, limited flat primary palette, absorbent paper stock
negative_add: photorealistic, smooth gradient, airbrush, anime, cel shading, 3d
works_for: Stills yes, video poorly. INFERRED from the flat-survives/texture-boils rule, not measured here: the dot screen is pixel-scale texture, which is the class LTX-2.3 boils, so a halftone keyframe tends to animate into a crawling moire. If you need it moving, hold the still and move the frame in post rather than letting i2v interpolate the dots.
note: Dot SCALE is the whole failure mode. Ask for coarse visible Ben-Day dots by name or the model renders a fine grey screen that disappears entirely at 1344x768, leaving a flat comic with no print idiom at all. NOT AVAILABLE on animagine: 'western comic' sits in this project's standing negative precisely because it returns anime eyes on comic anatomy (studio/tags/western_comic.json), so the tags field is deliberately empty rather than tempting. The anime checkpoint does have a native halftone idiom, but it is the Japanese one - 'manga, screentone, halftone, monochrome' gives screentone, a different style, and studio/tags/monochrome.json measured that monochrome greyscales the entire frame, so that route is black and white only. Do not mistake this for a look: the misregistration fringe has to be DRAWN, and no ffmpeg grade in studio/looks/ can add ink that was never printed.
verdict: On qwen a plain photo; on the illustration engine ordinary anime with no dot screen. Use manga_screentone, which actually produces tone.
